Summary (auto): Handoff between AE/SE and Blueline procurement/legal/security to align on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA targets, KMS requirements, and pricing approval pathway. Action items and timeline agreed.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining on a friday afternoon — appreciate it. quick roll call?
[00:06] Priya Rao: priya here, head of procurement at blueline.
[00:08] Daniel Kim: daniel, vp security.
[00:10] Sara Velasquez: sara from legal.
[00:11] Ethan Moore: ethan, data platform.
[00:14] Luca Patel: luca from redwood, solutions eng.
[00:16] Owen Brooks: owen, customer success — i'll be around for onboarding logistics.
[00:20] Maya Chen: cool, thanks. objective for today: run through the commercial-doc changes you asked for, make sure the SLA / KMS ask maps to our offering, and outline the procurement path — pricing committee steps. i'll hand to luca for the technical bits when we hit the KMS / private deployment questions.

[00:35] Priya Rao: great. to frame — procurement wants a clear checklist so we can move to finance approvals quickly. our timeline is tight: board sign-off target 2027-02-07. we need final commercial terms and any security exceptions by 2027-01-20 to hit that.
[00:48] Maya Chen: understood, that's tight but feasible. we'll prioritize the MSA/DPA redline and the SLA addendum.

[01:02] Sara Velasquez: quick note from legal: we will likely request stronger indemnity language around data breaches and explicit audit rights. also need clarity on subcontractors and any subprocessors. the MSA draft we saw had a general clause; we'd like a more prescriptive list or a process for notifying new subprocessors.
[01:25] Luca Patel: right, we can do a subprocessors appendix. luca — luca, sorry — that's something we can attach and keep updated. in practice, redwood uses a mix of cloud partners and dedicated services; we can provide a current list and a process to notify on changes.
[01:40] Daniel Kim: from security: our blocker is key management — we need either customer-managed KMS or HSM integration. we cannot have keys managed solely by the vendor for production PII processing. also, we need to know about encryption in transit at the token-level; does your streaming layer do end-to-end TLS? are there any proxies that terminate tls?
[02:05] Luca Patel: good questions. on KMS: we support customer-managed keys with KMS integrations in hosted mode — we can also offer Dedicated where keys stay in your VPC and you manage rotation via your cloud KMS/HSM. small caveat, the current hosted offering keeps model weights encrypted at rest with provider-managed keys unless you opt for private deployment.
[02:29] Ethan Moore: can you clarify the difference between hosted + CMK versus Dedicated private? because ops will want to know whether metadata still flows through redwood control plane.
[02:40] Maya Chen: yep — hosted with CMK means data and logs are encrypted with your key at rest, but control-plane metadata (billing, routing) still touches our control plane. in Dedicated/private deployments we can offer a customer-controlled control plane option so that metadata stays inside your VPC — luca can talk about hybrid routing.
[02:57] Luca Patel: for Dedicated we generally deploy the inference fleet in your cloud account or in a logically isolated tenancy; you can configure a private control plane option with API endpoints bound to your VPC. there are tradeoffs: uptime SLOs improve with dedicated capacity but procurement and on-boarding time increases.
[03:20] Priya Rao: procurement will want cost delta details. maya, you mentioned a pricing uplift for Dedicated — can we get a ballpark per-token or per-hour figure? finance wants to see sensitivity by QPS.
[03:35] Maya Chen: i'll send a region-by-region estimate. high level: Dedicated tends to be a 2.5x to 4x cost multiplier vs hosted for small teams because you're reserving capacity, but for sustained high QPS it often reduces unit cost. we'll include amortized GPU hours and licensing delta in the deck.
[03:50] Ethan Moore: (muttering) ok makes sense. i'll upload some traffic patterns to the shared sheet.

[04:05] Sara Velasquez: on SLAs — our legal folks want uptime SLO in the MSA and a clear credit structure. your template has a generic uptime clause. can you accept a 99.9% SLO for inference endpoints and a prescribed credit formula?
[04:25] Owen Brooks: we can commit to SLA targets, yes. luca, correct me if i'm wrong — we can do 99.9 for Dedicated on per-route basis, hosted is typically 99.5 but we can offer a tighter SLO for higher tiers.
[04:40] Luca Patel: that's accurate; also consider graceful degradation and fallbacks — you can specify fallback to a lower-cost model or regional failover in the routing policy. we also log request traces and can provide token-level latency breakdowns for incidents.
[04:58] Daniel Kim: what about audit logs and retention? we need immutable audit logs for two years and access to them for internal audits. is that available?
[05:08] Luca Patel: yes, audit logs can be exported to your s3/bucket or SIEM; retention windows are configurable and we can ship a copy to your storage for long-term retention. if you need immutability we can suggest an object-lock workflow in your bucket.
[05:20] Priya Rao: on DPA specifically — data residency. will logs or model outputs leave the eu region for eu customers? our compliance team insists data must remain in-eu unless otherwise authorized.
[05:34] Maya Chen: we have region-aware routing; for Blueline EU workloads we can pin inference to eu-west-1 and ensure storage stays in region for data at rest. for control plane messages there may be metadata that flows to our global mgmt plane; we can document that and provide contractual limitations.
[05:53] Sara Velasquez: ok please surface that in the DPA redline.

[06:05] Ethan Moore: a technical question — latency expectations. if we do dedicated in eu region, what's steady-state p95 for 2048-context generations?
[06:15] Luca Patel: on a single-request p95 we're seeing 120-180ms for optimized 2k contexts on the quantized variants on Ampere A100-class hardware in dedicated pools; numbers vary by model size. for bursty traffic we recommend autoscaling and pre-warmed nodes to keep p95 under 250ms.
[06:35] Ethan Moore: good. note for ops: average prompt size is ~900 tokens with embeddings and chunking. i'll add that to the shared sheet.

[06:50] Priya Rao: shifting back to procurement path — what does the approval chain look like at redwood for pricing exceptions and commitment terms? we may want a 12-month reserved capacity with quarterly true-ups.
[07:02] Maya Chen: we have a few lanes: self-serve marketing lists are standard; for reserved capacity and enterprise terms we have a pricing committee — i can route a formal proposal to finance and get approval window estimates. typically 5-7 business days after we submit the redline and the commercial sheet.
[07:20] Sara Velasquez: legal will likely have redlines on liability caps, indemnities, and data breach notice periods. what flexibility do you have on liability cap for PII processing?
[07:33] Maya Chen: standard cap is tied to fees paid in prior 12 months. we can discuss carve-outs for gross negligence and will review with legal. luca, can we signal which clauses are hard stops?
[07:42] Luca Patel: yes, we can highlight non-negotiables. typically IP and export controls are firm; a few security controls are negotiable with compensating controls. we'll mark them in the redline.

[08:00] Daniel Kim: one more — encryption key rotation frequency. if we bring our own key we want automated rotation every 90 days and ability to revoke at will. is online key rotation supported or is there a planned downtime window?
[08:13] Luca Patel: rotation is supported online for CMK-backed storage. for HSM-backed private deployments key rotation can be managed in your HSM; revocation semantics depend on your HSM and the cluster's key caching window. we can provide recommended rotation windows and a mechanism for immediate revocation that will invalidate new sessions while allowing a short cache expiry for in-flight requests.
[08:41] Ethan Moore: that's fine — we'll test revocation behavior during the pilot.

[08:50] Priya Rao: any vendor questionnaire we need to fill out? our security team uses a standard 200-question infosec vendor form.
[08:58] Owen Brooks: yes, we can take that. please drop the vendor security questionnaire into the shared folder and i'll have our security ops owner triage. luca will own high-level infra answers.
[09:10] Maya Chen: i'll add our SOC2 summary and fedramp pathway notes. note: we don't claim fedramp yet but we've done initial readiness and can share the plan.

[09:25] Sara Velasquez: about subprocessors list — please include any analytics or telemetry providers. we need transparency on third-party tracing and APM providers.
[09:36] Luca Patel: yes, will include APM and telemetry. some names may be slightly mis-transcribed in earlier decks; we'll make sure the redline has correct vendor names.

[09:50] Priya Rao: can we recap next steps and owners?
[09:55] Maya Chen: sure. recapping: luca will produce a redline MSA/DPA with subprocessors appendix and highlight negotiable vs non-negotiable clauses by 2027-01-13. maya will send pricing deck with Dedicated vs Hosted comparisons and per-region estimates by 2027-01-11. blueline (ethan) will fill traffic patterns and QPS into the shared sheet by 2027-01-14. daniel will send KMS/HSM vendor list and rotation policy by 2027-01-15. sara will provide legal summary of top 5 redlines by 2027-01-12. owen will coordinate vendor questionnaire intake.
[10:28] Priya Rao: sounds good. procurement wants a single doc that shows go/no-go items so we can fast-track finance.
[10:35] Maya Chen: we'll make a one-page procurement checklist and include that in the packet.

[10:45] Daniel Kim: final ask — can you provide an on-record contact for incident response and a POC for SOC2 artifacts review?
[10:54] Maya Chen: yes, incident response contact is security-ops@redwood.com; for SOC2 artifact review luca will coordinate with our security team and we can set up a time next week for a readout.
[11:05] Sara Velasquez: ok, thanks everyone. i may have follow-ups but we'll look for the redline and the procurement packet.
[11:12] Maya Chen: perfect — thanks all. we'll follow up with the materials and lock in the dedicated feasibility call for the week of jan 18.
[11:20] Meeting end
